findings: The section is printed as 14.1.2 but belongs under 14.2 (14.2.2); recorded and noted in the lesson.

The book says the hypothalamus signals the posterior pituitary 'to create a sensation of thirst'; thirst is produced by the hypothalamus's thirst centre and the posterior pituitary releases ADH. The lesson attributes thirst to the hypothalamus, flagged.

The tidbits on ADH and blood pressure and on aldosterone and hyperkalaemia, and the two capillary beds, are carried in the lesson. Original figure archived as c12-bio-ch14-fig-urine-formation (drawn for this lesson; not the textbook's picture).
